notes: 20 stone lines, numbered (2)-(20) in the type. Griffith's English: Malewitar, born of Shayakeli (?), begotten of the anashayi in Shaye; qeren-akrere, qeren of Nakazeye, wemanis-akrere, chief envoy of Rome, envoy of Makheye, nate of the envoy-law qerete of Makheye, yazi ashakhayaki (?) yeteke, shashi-mete-maleyes, envoy in Khalite, khalben in Khalite, ....s shaqake (?), kin of the kharpkhan in Pakharas Atapete, kin of the shi....-akrere Shibawiye, kin of ateqis in Shazes, of belilekes in Pezeme, of tartekeses in Taketere, of maleyeses in Atiye; formulae A B C, extended invocation to Isis and Mak-lakh, formula E. His queries (? printed over the sign): y and l of syekeli; k, y, a of asḫyki and i of ydi; ḫ and l of ḫlbeñ; a and p of akilopkri; q, o and the lost sign of qo[.]ẖdḫ[.]y; q of sqkelowi; the restored divider after kḫẖḫsel; e of atpete; to of si[.]ḫẖn[...]to; l and te of t(15)ketoreteleb and of atiyeteleb; y of yiẖekete; p of p[s]ḫrkete. His note to l. 8: for qo[.]ẖdḫ[.]y '[.]kroro might perhaps be read'. In [a]potelw only the second stroke of a is bracketed; the whole sign is bracketed here. His formula table (p. 60) prints formula B as p[si]ḫrkete (s and i restored) where the text has p[s]ḫrkete; its A, C and E agree with the text, and the p. 59 table confirms q (not w) in qetrri. Printed spaces kept as printed inside words known as one: 'te rikelowi', 'ye tekelowi', 'sibwi ye'. Every 3-shaped sign was decided at 3.5-4x beside sure examples on the page: m narrow and smooth, ẖ wide with a pointed middle (ẖ in apotelẖ, mẖeyot, ẖlite-, ẖdḫ, kḫẖḫsel, ẖ[...]se, pẖrse, ḫẖn, mẖe, ẖolkete, mklẖ, ẖolketese). No sign left uncertain by me. ' | ' marks each line of Griffith's type (he sets one phrase per type line; an overflow printed right-aligned on the next line is joined to its line); (n) is his superscript stone-line number, kept where printed; [x] his restoration; [.] a lost sign (hatched); [...] his dots.

notes: 12 stone lines per Griffith; the type numbers (2)-(10). Griffith: 'The lettering is exceedingly incorrect', probably a foreigner's monument. His English: the honourable Tebishi-lakh, truly begotten of the chief qeren in Qereti (?) Patenete, truly born of Tasayishe (?), kin of strategi and envoys; O Mak-lakh; formulae B C; Male. 'sic' over the second o of apoteoleb and over the m of 'am' (for at, formula B). In tseyis·e the middle dot marks two signs, s (Griffith's š) + e, not the se sign. His formula table (p. 60) prints B as posiḫrkete with 'sic' over o, where the text (checked at 3.5x) has pi(9)siḫrkete. notes: Griffith describes ten lines between rules, but his type numbers stone lines (2)-(12). Two deceased, plural formulae. His English: O Isis, O Osiris, O Mak-lakh; Yerekiñamarakhali and Beke-lakhali, truly born of the kelkeni Matalabe, truly begotten of the chief shamat Qarkili, kin of the shashi-mete pelametareyes Amanap-tame and the bes (?) Khabeye, kin of the malakeyes Tepeye-tamite; formulae A B C. His notes: l. 4, for smt-lh cf. Kar. 52, Shab. 4, 'the m always uncertain'; l. 8, mlkeyose 'belonging to the malakeye (?)', cf. 132/4. His queries: ẖ of yerekiñmrẖli, m of smtlẖ, ẖ of ẖboye. Overflow lines joined: tedḫe + lebkwi (stone l. 4), yetmde + lebkwi (l. 9). His formula table (p. 60) agrees with A, B and C here.
